extra.message: Remote code execution via exec() on user input — Attacker can execute arbitrary Python code on the server, leading to full server compromise (file write demonstrated via p0wned.txt) [verified: first_name is base64-decoded and passed directly to exec() with no sandboxing or restriction.]

Remote code execution via exec() on user-supplied base64 payload — Arbitrary Python code execution on the server, full compromise of the application process (file write demonstrated via p0wned.txt, but any code can run). [verified: duplicate of idx 1 — exec() on base64-decoded POST data with no sandboxing.]

DEBUG=True hardcoded in settings — Full information disclosure of source code, local variables, request data, and Django settings (including SECRET_KEY) via Django's debug error page [verified: DEBUG=True is hardcoded and not env-gated, so any unhandled exception (e.g. boom) discloses full stack traces, local vars, and settings including SECRET_KEY to anonymous users.]

CSRF protection middleware disabled globally — Any state-changing POST endpoint in the app can be triggered cross-site without a token, enabling attacker-forged requests against any user's session [verified: CsrfViewMiddleware is commented out globally, removing CSRF protection app-wide for all POST endpoints, consistent with the app's intentionally-vulnerable design.]

Path traversal / arbitrary file read via user_pic — Attacker can read arbitrary files on the server filesystem (e.g. /etc/passwd, source code, settings.py containing SECRET_KEY) by supplying '../' sequences or an absolute path in the p parameter [verified: filename from request.GET flows unsanitized into os.path.join and open(); only a try/except catches IOError, no path validation exists.]

IDOR — unauthenticated cross-user profile read/write — Any anonymous client can view or modify any other user's profile data (including the admin user's) by changing the userid in the URL [verified: dor_user_profile has no session/ownership check; any userid can be read or overwritten via POST.]

Missing function-level access control on admin view — Any unauthenticated user can access admin-only functionality/content by setting action=admin [verified: missing_access_control gates admin template solely on a client-supplied action=admin GET param with no auth check.]

Unvalidated forward / arbitrary function invocation via globals() lookup — Attacker can invoke any function defined in the module namespace (e.g. boom, admin, or others) by name, bypassing intended navigation/access flow and potentially triggering unintended code paths [verified: fwd is looked up in globals() and called with no whitelist, allowing invocation of any module-level function.]

Unvalidated forward / arbitrary function invocation via globals() lookup — Attacker can invoke any module-level callable in the views module (e.g. reach the 'admin' view directly bypassing intended navigation, or trigger unexpected views), broadening the attack surface and enabling access-control bypass. [verified: duplicate of idx 3 — globals() lookup and call with no target whitelist.]

Debug toolbar exposed via user-controlled cookie/param — Unauthenticated attacker can enable verbose debug introspection (SQL, settings, SECRET_KEY, environment) by simply sending a cookie or query param [verified: show_toolbar reads an attacker-controlled cookie/param with no auth check to gate a debug tool that exposes SQL/settings/SECRET_KEY, and DEBUG=True makes this reachable.]

Reflected XSS via qs parameter reflected into templates — Attacker-crafted qs value rendered in the page can execute in the victim's browser context if the corresponding template disables escaping, enabling session/cookie theft or actions as the victim [verified: templates form.html and query.html render {{qs|safe}} confirming autoescaping is explicitly disabled for user-controlled qs.]

Reflected XSS via qs/path parameters — If the corresponding templates disable autoescaping or use |safe (as is standard for this exercise's 'vulnerable' variant), attacker-controlled script executes in the victim's browser session, enabling cookie theft (note the 'monster' cookie set without HttpOnly) or session hijacking. [verified: confirmed via template grep: query.html and path.html both use {{qs|safe}}/{{path|safe}}, disabling autoescape for user input.]

CSRF protection disabled on state-reflecting endpoint — Cross-site requests can trigger this endpoint on behalf of an authenticated victim without a CSRF token, and combined with the XSS sink this enables classic CSRF-to-XSS chaining used in the exercise. [verified: csrf_image is explicitly decorated with @csrf_exempt and reflects qs via |safe, removing CSRF protection on a state-adjacent/XSS-chainable endpoint.]

Open redirect via unvalidated_redirect — Attacker can craft links that appear to originate from the trusted domain but redirect victims to attacker-controlled phishing sites [verified: url from request.GET passed directly to redirect() with no whitelist/relative-path check.]

Information disclosure via unhandled exception / debug page — Exposes stack traces, source code snippets, file paths, and potentially settings values (SECRET_KEY) if DEBUG=True [verified: boom() raises an unhandled exception with no try/except; exploitability depends on DEBUG=True but is the app's stated exercise design.]
